title: Week 25 Reading Quiz
description_html: Read both lessons before you start. Choose the best answer for each question. You may take this quiz twice, and your higher score counts.

questions.name: Question 1
questions.text_html: The English words ranch, rodeo, corral, lariat, and mustang all come from Spanish. What does this suggest about the Texas cowboy?

answers.text: He invented ranching without any help, and learned nothing at all from the people before him.
He learned his trade only from German settlers.
He first learned to ranch in the Rocky Mountains.
Much of his skill and vocabulary came from the vaquero tradition.

questions.name: Question 2
questions.text_html: Richard King bought land in South Texas and brought whole families of vaqueros from a Mexican village to work it. What does this show?

answers.text: Anglo ranchers had no cattle of their own and had to hire vaqueros to raise any at all.
Vaqueros were forced to leave Mexico by a treaty.
Anglo ranchers relied on vaquero skill and borrowed their methods.
The King Ranch was first a German farming village.

questions.name: Question 3
questions.text_html: German farmers in the Hill Country built stone houses and fences and raised fewer cattle on fenced land. How did they differ from open-range ranchers?

answers.text: They raised no animals of any kind, and lived only on the grain that they grew on their land.
They moved their herds each spring on long drives all the way to Kansas.
They avoided building towns and kept apart from one another's farms.
They worked smaller farms and fenced their land instead of letting herds roam.

questions.name: Question 4
questions.text_html: J. Frank Dobie wrote books like The Longhorns. What does the lesson say he contributed?

answers.text: He invented the cowboy hat and the rope, and taught the vaqueros how to use them on the range.
He taught the vaqueros how to rope and brand cattle on the range.
He wrote down the stories of old ranch hands so later readers could learn them.
He founded the Texas Rangers in the 1820s with Stephen F. Austin.

questions.name: Question 5
questions.text_html: Raiding parties usually vanished before Rangers arrived, even when the Rangers camped near a settlement. What does this suggest?

answers.text: The Rangers had no horses at all, and could patrol only on foot in the country near the forts.
The frontier was huge, and raiders who knew the ground could move faster than the Rangers.
The raiders had no reason to flee because Rangers never gave chase.
The settlers never reported any thefts to the Rangers or to anyone else.

questions.name: Question 6
questions.text_html: Many Texas slaveholders demanded that Mexico return enslaved people who crossed the Rio Grande, and Mexico refused. What fact explains Mexico's refusal?

answers.text: Mexico had no army to send to the border.
The treaty of 1848 required Mexico to refuse.
Slavery was against the law in Mexico.
The Rio Grande was not yet a border between the countries.

questions.name: Question 7
questions.text_html: Many Tejanos saw Juan Cortina as a defender, while many Texans saw him as a bandit. Which fact helps explain the Tejano view?

answers.text: Many Tejano families had lost land to lawyers, taxes, or threats, and thought it unfair.
Cortina had once been a Texas Ranger captain, and many Texans trusted him to protect the frontier.
Cortina wanted Texas to leave the Union and join Mexico in 1859.
Cortina refused to fight at all when he reached the town of Brownsville.
